page.h1: HTS Chapter 34: Soap, organic surface-active agents, washing preparations, lubricating preparations, artificial waxes, prepared waxes, polishing or scouring preparations, candles and similar articles, modeling pastes, "dental waxes" and dental preparations with a basis of plaster — U.S. Exports & Foreign Tariffs

seo.title: U.S. Soap, Detergent & Lubricant Exports and Foreign Tariffs (HTS Ch. 34) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: U.S. exports of soap, detergents, lubricants, waxes and candles were $8.41B in 2025. Who buys them (Canada 37%), what sells, and which buyers charge more: China.

intro:
The U.S. exported **$8.41B** of soap, detergents, lubricating preparations, waxes, polishes and candles in 2025, 1.3% more than in 2024. Surfactants, laundry and dish detergents and cleaners (3402) were **46%** of it, lubricating preparations such as greases, cutting oils and synthetic lubricants (3403) 25%, and soap and liquid hand soap (3401) 14%. Canada alone took **37%** and Mexico 10%. In January–August 2026 exports were $5.65B, 1% less than in the same months of 2025.

Most large buyers charge nothing on U.S. goods: Canada and Mexico under USMCA, Singapore, Korea under KORUS, and the EU on the whole chapter since July 1, 2026. **China** is the exception: on top of its normal 6.5–10% rate it adds a 10% extra tariff on all U.S. goods and its 2018–2019 counter-tariffs of 5–25%, so U.S. lubricants pay **45%** there. Canada charged a 25% surtax on U.S. soaps from March 4 to August 31, 2025, but nothing in this chapter is on its 2026 list. Beyond tariffs, chemical registration in the buyer's market (REACH in the EU, K-REACH in Korea, China's new-substance registration) decides access, covered on the Markets page.

stats.note: China; Canada's 2025 soap surtax was removed

keyTakeaways: Canada, the largest buyer at $3.11B, charges nothing on U.S. Chapter 34 goods that qualify for CUSMA. Its 25% surtax on U.S. soaps (3401) ran only from March 4 to August 31, 2025, and its September 2026 counter-tariff list names no Chapter 34 goods.

In China, U.S. lubricating preparations (3403.19, 3403.99) and non-ionic surfactants (3402.42) pay about 45% and 41.5%: a normal rate of 10% or 6.5%, a 25% counter-tariff from 2018 and the 10% extra on all U.S. goods. Their product exclusion ran out on February 28, 2025, and U.S. sales to China fell 9% in 2025.

The EU cut its duty on all U.S. Chapter 34 goods to zero from July 1, 2026, removing 4% on detergents and surfactants and 4.6–6.5% on lubricants. Its 2025 counter-tariff list named nearly the whole chapter at 10–30% but was never applied.
Two China dates matter: its market-based exclusions end on December 31, 2026, and its extra tariff could rise from 10% to 34% on January 10, 2027.
